edges.description: Loss of the activating enzyme leaves substrate intact but product absent.
Combined calcium and phosphate deficit lowers the calcium-phosphate product at the mineralization front.

nodes.description: Absent calcitriol removes the ligand for the vitamin D receptor in the intestine, reducing active calcium absorption. Serum calcium falls, parathyroid hormone rises, and parathyroid hormone-driven phosphaturia adds a phosphate deficit, so the mineralization front is short of both ions. This is the disorder-specific instance of the module's calciopenic trigger arm; the substitution relative to the generic module node is that the interruption sits at 1-alpha-hydroxylation rather than at intake, 25-hydroxylation, or the receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic and Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Vitamin D Dependent Rickets Type 1A.
evidence.snippet: Seven patients had mild hypocalcemia at presentation while four patients had normal calcium concentrations.

nodes.description: Physiological replacement with the missing hormone, calcitriol, or with alfacalcidol which requires only hepatic 25-hydroxylation to become active. This bypasses the enzymatic block rather than overwhelming it, which is why physiological rather than pharmacological doses suffice and why the disorder is termed vitamin D-dependent.

Hydroxyapatite is not deposited into newly formed osteoid, and in the open growth plates of infancy the hypertrophic chondrocyte layer expands, producing the widened, cupped and frayed metaphyses of rickets together with bone pain, deformity of the weight-bearing long bones, and growth failure.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic and Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Vitamin D Dependent Rickets Type 1A.
evidence.snippet: VDDR1A should definitely be considered when a patient with signs of rickets has a normal 25-OHD level or when there is unresponsiveness to vitamin D treatment.

nodes.description: CYP27B1 encodes the mitochondrial cytochrome P450 that carries out the final, rate-limiting activation step of vitamin D, 1-alpha-hydroxylation of 25-hydroxyvitamin D in the renal proximal tubule. Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish this activity. Because the preceding hepatic 25-hydroxylation is intact, 25-hydroxyvitamin D is normal or elevated while calcitriol is low - the biochemical signature that separates this disorder from nutritional rickets and from CYP2R1 disease.

evidence.reference_title: Cloning of human 25-hydroxyvitamin D-1 alpha-hydroxylase and mutations causing vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1.
evidence.snippet: Primary cultures of human adult and neonatal keratinocytes exhibit abundant 1 alpha-hydroxylase activity, whereas those from a patient with VDDR-1 lacked detectable activity.

evidence.reference_title: Cloning of human 25-hydroxyvitamin D-1 alpha-hydroxylase and mutations causing vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1.
evidence.snippet: The key step in the biosynthesis of 1,25(OH)2D is its 1 alpha-hydroxylation from 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD) in the kidney.
